note: Hebrew nissah means to test or prove; in 1611 "tempt" could mean test, but today it implies enticing to sin, which the text does not say (cf. Jas 1:13). Context: test (high confidence). 22:12 'now I know that you fear God' states the purpose: a test of loyalty.

kjv: God will provide himself a lamb
mine: God will see to the lamb for himself
note: Hebrew yir'eh-lo hasseh is "will see for himself the lamb", i.e. provide it; the KJV word order invites the reading that God provides himself as the lamb, which the Hebrew does not express.
The name YHWH yir'eh means "Yahweh will see (to it)"; the KJV transliterates it with the hybrid form Jehovah, obscuring the wordplay with v.8 and the saying that follows.

kjv: shall all the nations of the earth be blessed
mine: all the nations of the earth shall bless themselves
note: The verb is hithpael (hitbarakhu), normally reflexive: nations will invoke Abraham's offspring in blessing; the KJV follows the passive of the LXX (and Gal 3:8), unlike the niphal in 12:3.
